title: Towards Quantization-Aware Training for Ultra-Low-Bit Reasoning LLMs
claim: Existing QAT fine-tunes on pre-training data and loses reasoning ability; ours calibrates on mixed domains and uses RL-inspired fine-tuning to retain it.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right flow, shared FP16 source, robot outcome icons
description: A horizontal two-row diagram. On the left, an FP16 robot with a 2x2 grid of original weights (0.1, 0.5, 1.3, -0.2) labeled as having strong reasoning ability. Thick black arrows lead to two pipelines. The top row, titled 'Existing QAT Pipeline', uses a calibration box containing only pre-training data. It runs quantization (1st stage) to a 2x2 grid of ternary weights, then supervised fine-tuning (2nd stage) to fine-tuned weights. These feed an INT2 robot that says 'I'm stumped...' and is labeled 'Weak Reasoning Ability' in red. The bottom row, titled 'Our Proposed QAT Pipeline' in blue, uses calibration boxes with mixed pre-training and reasoning data (code, math). It runs quantization, then a blue RL-inspired fine-tuning arrow, giving an INT2 robot that says 'I've got this! First, ...' labeled 'Strong Reasoning Ability' in green. A reasoning-task prompt box sits in the middle right, with inference arrows pointing to both robots.
caption: Comparison of the existing QAT pipeline with the proposed pipeline.
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable performance across diverse reasoning tasks, yet their deployment is hindered by prohibitive computational and memory costs. Quantization-aware training (QAT) enables ultra-low-bit compression (<4 bits per weight), but existing QAT methods often degrade reasoning capability, partly because complex knowledge structures are introduced during the post-training process in LLMs. In this paper, through a systematic investigation of how quantization affects different data domains, we find that its impact on pre-training and reasoning capabilities differs. Building on this insight, we propose a novel two-stage QAT pipeline specifically designed for reasoning LLMs. In the first stage, we quantize the model using mixed-domain calibration data to preserve essential capabilities across domains; in the second stage, we fine-tune the quantized model with a teacher-guided reward-rectification loss to restore reasoning capability. We first demonstrate that mixed-domain calibration outperforms single-domain calibration by up to 2.74% improvement on average over six tasks, including reasoning and pre-trained tasks. Following experiments on five reasoning benchmarks show that our 2-bit-quantized Qwen3-8B outperforms post-training quantization (PTQ) baselines by 50.45% on average. Moreover, compared to ultra-low-bit-specialized models such as BitNet-2B4T, our pipeline achieves approximately 2\% higher mathematical-reasoning accuracy with fewer than 1B tokens. Code is available: https://github.com/yasu0001/ReasoningQAT
